headline: Reflection AI's new Beam coding model scores ahead of a US rival but behind some Chinese open models in published comparisons, and its promised download is still pending.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 1: the unveiling was on 5 Oct and already ran on 6 Oct; the new details are mostly the company's own scores.
importance_line: Developers, governments and companies that want a US-built AI they can run on their own systems get a possible option, but the scores are Reflection's own, Beam is open only to selected users and a waitlist for now, and the promised download and safety results are still due.
summary: WinBuzzer reports, from Reflection's own scorecard, that Beam, the first coding model from the US startup Reflection AI, scores 80.1 on Terminal Bench v2.1 (a test of tasks done through a computer's command line), ahead of Inkling, a US rival from Thinking Machines Lab, at 63.8 but behind Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 at 88.3. Beam was unveiled on 5 Oct 2026 and carried in our 6 Oct 2026 edition from TechCrunch; new today are these comparisons, and Beam's free-to-download weights (the trained settings others can run themselves) are still promised only for later in October.
notes: Read WinBuzzer in full. Continues our 6 Oct 2026 entry (TechCrunch) on Beam's unveiling. Scores are Reflection's own or other vendors' own results under different test settings; WinBuzzer says they are not a controlled comparison.
